pages.quiz:
PHYSICS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 10
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

2. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Petrol fires have no fuel
   D. Water always increases oxygen

3. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Moments and equilibrium? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Moments and equilibrium.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Moments and equilibrium.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Moments and equilibrium.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Waves? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Waves.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Waves.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Waves.

6. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Pressure? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Pressure.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Pressure.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Pressure.

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Energy, Work, Power and Machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Energy, Work, Power and Machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Energy, Work, Power and Machines.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Electronics? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Electronics.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Electronics.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Electronics.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Electronics.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Physics? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Physics.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Physics.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Physics.

12. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Producers
   D. Primary consumers only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Temperature and Thermal Expansion and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Moments and equilibrium and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Energy, Work, Power and Machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Waves and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — 100 °C

2. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

3. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

4. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Moments and equilibrium.

5. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Waves.

6. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Pressure.

8. A — Ice melting to water

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Energy, Work, Power and Machines.

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Electronics.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Physics.

12. C — Producers

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Temperature and Thermal Expansion; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Energy, Work, Power and Machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
